title: Cranberry and orange tart
subtitle: festive cranberry orange curd tart
excerpt: A cranberry and orange tart has a vivid, jewel-coloured curd filling made from fresh cranberries cooked with orange juice and zest, then strained and enriched with eggs and butter. The curd is bright, sharp, and deeply coloured, cranberry-red in the tin, it sets to a dense, sliceable filling with a flavour somewhere between cranberry sauce and a sharp citrus curd. This is a strong winter tart that holds up against rich Christmas food.
sourceNotes: Cranberry and orange is one of the most canonical North American winter flavour pairings, appearing in cranberry sauce, glazes, and drinks. The application to a curd tart follows the same method as lemon curd tart (tarte au citron) but uses the acidity of cranberries rather than lemon juice. Cranberry curd has become increasingly common in American home baking from around 2010 onward as a Thanksgiving and Christmas alternative to lemon curd; it reached mainstream British domestic baking slightly later.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best made the day before; the curd firms and the flavour deepens overnight.
recipe.temperatureNote: for blind baking the pastry case only

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: 190°C conventional for blind baking; the cranberry curd is cooked on the hob

content.text: Cranberry and orange tart uses a deeply coloured cranberry curd that looks striking and tastes sharp and fruity. The cranberries are cooked first to extract their juice, then strained before the eggs and butter go in, the same technique as making any fruit curd, but producing a colour more vivid than lemon.

Make, chill, and roll the pastry to 3 mm. Line a 23 cm loose-bottomed tart tin, refrigerate 20 minutes, then blind bake at 190°C with beans for 15 minutes and without for 10 minutes until fully baked through. Cool completely.

Put the cranberries, orange juice, and zest in a medium saucepan with 50 g of the sugar. Cook over a medium heat for about 8 minutes, stirring, until all the cranberries have burst and the mixture is thick and jammy. Press through a fine sieve into a clean saucepan, pushing firmly to extract all the liquid. Discard the skins and seeds left in the sieve.
Make the curd and fill the case

Add the remaining 125 g sugar to the strained cranberry liquid and bring back to a gentle simmer. Whisk the eggs in a bowl, then pour the warm cranberry mixture over them in a steady stream, whisking constantly. Return everything to the saucepan over a low heat, stirring constantly for about 8 minutes until thickened to a custardy consistency. Remove from the heat and stir in the butter piece by piece until melted. Pour into the cooled pastry case and refrigerate for at least 2 hours until set firm.
